sections.heading: Do British citizens need a Nigeria visa?
sections.text: British passport holders need a visa to visit Nigeria. Since May 2025, short visits such as tourism, business and visiting family can be applied for online as a Nigeria eVisa, with decisions usually within 48 hours.

sections.heading: Nigeria eVisa or regular visa?
sections.text:
Nigeria offers two ways to apply for short visits:
- The eVisa: fully online, decided in about 48 hours, single entry, valid for 30 to 90 days and not extendable. Best for one-off trips.
- The regular visa: applied for online and completed at a visa application appointment in the UK. Best for longer stays and repeat trips, especially for business.

For working in Nigeria, you need the STR work visa or a Temporary Work Permit. Choose the option that matches your trip above.

sections.heading: Nigeria visa for other passport holders
sections.text: UK residents on other passports apply the same way unless their nationality is exempt, such as ECOWAS countries. Longer stays and work need a different visa.

sections.heading: Nigeria eVisa: key facts
sections.text: The eVisa is applied for entirely online through the Nigeria Immigration Service. It's single entry, valid for between 30 and 90 days depending on the type, and can't be extended. You'll also need a yellow fever vaccination certificate, and to complete Nigeria's online health declaration before you fly.

sections.heading: Documents for a Nigeria eVisa
sections.text: You'll usually need your passport photo page, a recent photo, your return flight booking, proof of accommodation or an invitation letter from your host in Nigeria, and recent bank statements.

sections.heading: Nigeria visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and handle Nigeria visa applications for travellers across the UK, entirely online. We check the current rules for your nationality, complete your application and keep you updated until it's approved. Before you travel, read the UK government's [foreign travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice) for Nigeria.

faqs.q: How long does a Nigeria eVisa take?
faqs.a: Decisions are usually made within 48 hours, but apply at least a week before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I extend a Nigeria eVisa?
faqs.a: No. The eVisa can't be extended, so choose the right length for your trip.

faqs.q: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Nigeria?
faqs.a: Yes, a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate is required for entry.
